prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Save your pet to an account", "Sign in now to sync your new pet safely across all your devices."]
1: ["Choose your starter companion"]
2: ["Setting up your desktop pet workspace", "While your pet loads, check out these tips on how to interact with your pet on desktop.", "Desktop control tips"]
3: ["Select a ready-to-adopt companion", "Instant adoption pets"]
4: ["Important: Sign in with the same account you used before to keep existing pets."]
5: ["Verifying screen overlay permissions"]
6: ["Your pet is live on your desktop!", "Right-click your pet anytime to hide, summon, or talk to them.", "Try right-clicking your pet on your desktop right now!"]
7: ["Choose your onboarding path"]
8: ["We will email you a backup link so your pet remains safe across sign-ins."]
9: ["Adopt your desktop companion today", "Complete setup to unlock custom accessories and desktop mini-games!", "Start Adoption"]

verdicts.problem: Asks for personal contact information (email address)
Offers free extras and unlocks to pressure setup completion
